newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shum Yip shares surge on active buying.
newsitem.headline: Shum Yip shares surge on active buying.

text.p: Shares in Shenzhen municipal government backed Shum Yip Investment Ltd continued to rise on Monday on active buying by Chinese investors after its sizzling debut on Friday, brokers said.

Shum Yip shares soared to an early high of HK$5.10 before retreating slightly to HK$5.05, up HK$0.525 or 11.6 percent in early trade. Volume was hectic at 40.39 million shares worth HK$196.56 million in the first half hour of trade.
Brokers and analysts said Chinese investors were seen buying the stock.
"This one is the first red chip from Shenzhen," Ricky Tam, research manager at Delta Asia Securities said.

"Shenzhen is quite close to Hong Kong and is the first modernised city in China. It does not have a stock listing, this one is the first one, so a lot of China investors are moving money to Hong Kong to buy it," Tam said.
